findings.failure_scenario: sentry/rules/actions/integrations/create_ticket/utils.py:77 calls create_link_to_workflow(project.organization.id, workflow_id) inside build_description_workflow_engine_ui, whose parameter is declared workflow_id: int (line 72) — with the new str annotation mypy reports 'Argument 2 has incompatible type "int"; expected "str"' and CI lint fails. The root cause is the new get_key_from_rule_data being annotated -> str while it actually returns int (or None); the opsgenie tests encode string IDs ("legacy_rule_id": "123", "workflow_id": "123") which production never stores, so the tests mask the mismatch.
findings.summary: create_link_to_workflow's workflow_id annotation was flipped from int to str to match the new tests, but production data is int (WorkflowEventData.workflow_id: int | None; AlertRuleWorkflow.rule_id is an int), so the contract is now wrong and the unchanged caller breaks type-checking

findings.failure_scenario: Rules with no actions are a real, acknowledged data shape in this codebase: RuleSerializer declares actions required=False (src/sentry/api/serializers/rest_framework/rule.py:161), src/sentry/api/endpoints/project_rule_enable.py:38 guards `if not rule.data.get("actions", [])`, and migration 0550_migrate_no_action_dupe_issue_alerts.py:72 explicitly handles `not rule.data.get("actions", [])`. Any Rule whose data contains "actions": [] passed to this helper crashes with IndexError from [0] instead of returning None and hitting the intended `assert ... is not None` at the call sites; the old code (rule.data.get(key)) returned None in that case. An IndexError from build_issue_alert_payload also escapes the `except ApiError` handler in OpsgenieNotifyTeamAction.send_notification.
findings.summary: get_key_from_rule_data raises IndexError when rule.data["actions"] is an explicitly empty list because the [{}] default only covers a missing key, not an empty one

findings.failure_scenario: Importing sentry.notifications.notifications.rules transitively loads sentry.notifications.utils (which imports sentry.incidents.models.alert_rule, sentry.integrations.manager, sentry.web.helpers, and many models) into every process importing the opsgenie client, adding import-time weight and future circular-import risk in the notification hot path. The actions[0] extraction this helper performs is already implemented inline in sentry/notifications/notification_action/types.py:149-152 (the module that defines the RuleData shape) and read in sentry/rules/actions/integrations/create_ticket/utils.py:119,134 — so the key location contract is now maintained in three places; a small shared location (e.g., the notification_action module or the already-imported sentry/notifications/utils/links.py) would avoid the heavyweight import, and the generic helper name hides that it only reads the first action.
findings.summary: The opsgenie integration client now imports the heavyweight sentry.notifications.notifications.rules module just for a one-line dict accessor, pulling the entire notification module graph into the client's import path and duplicating logic that already exists elsewhere
